Before an asset has data, AS's convention elsewhere is to split the portfolio evenly among available assets (not stated specifically for Ivy) (uncertain).

plain_english: A simple endowment-style buy & hold portfolio: one fifth each in US stocks, foreign stocks, Treasuries, real estate and commodities. Nothing is ever timed; the only activity is periodically resetting the five slices back to 20%.
notes: AS has no dedicated public post on its Ivy Portfolio. Evidence it is the static equal-weight version: (1) AS's 2019 public strategy-asset matrix lists Ivy with DBC, EFA, IEF, SPY, VNQ and NO cash column, whereas GTAA 5 has the same five plus Cash; (2) AS lists Ivy among its buy & hold portfolios (All-Weather, Permanent, Golden Butterfly); (3) in AS monthly performance tables, Ivy and GTAA 5 returns nearly coincide in months when GTAA 5 was likely fully invested (e.g. Oct-2017 1.35% vs 1.35%) but diverge sharply when GTAA 5 was partly in cash (e.g. Dec-2018 -4.74% vs -2.76%; Jan-2019 +6.85% vs +0.27%), i.e. Ivy has no trend filter. The book itself also presents the 10-month SMA timing overlay (that tactical version is tracked separately by AS as GTAA 5) and larger Ivy 10/Ivy 20 versions; AS appears to use only the 5-asset version. Rebalance frequency for AS's Ivy is not stated publicly (uncertain). Book ETF tickers not verified (book not accessible); AS conforms to its representative ETFs regardless.

name: Global Tactical Asset Allocation 5 (GTAA 5)
author: Mebane Faber

source.title: A Quantitative Approach to Tactical Asset Allocation (Journal of Wealth Management 2007; SSRN working paper 2006, updated Feb 2009 and Feb 2013)

rebalance: monthly; signal at the close of the last trading day of the month, traded at that same close; entire portfolio rebalanced to fixed slices every month even with no signal change
signal: TREND_i = 1 if P_i,t > SMA10_i,t else 0, where P = dividend-adjusted (total return) close on the last trading day of month t and SMA10 = arithmetic mean of the 10 most recent month-end adjusted closes including month t.
rules: Assign a fixed 20% slice to each of five assets: SPY (US equities), EFA (intl developed equities; IEFA from 2025), IEF (US 7-10y Treasuries), VNQ (US REITs), DBC (commodities; PDBC stitched on from ~Dec 2022).
At the close on the last trading day of each month compute each asset's 10-month SMA of month-end adjusted closes (current month-end included).
If an asset's month-end close is above its 10-month SMA, hold that asset at 20%; otherwise put that 20% slice in cash (T-bills, BIL).
Slices are independent: an asset's weight never depends on the others, and a failing slice is never redistributed to other assets.
Hold until the last trading day of the following month; rebalance all slices back to 20% monthly regardless of signal changes.

pre_etf_proxies.note: Faber's data; AS uses its own (undisclosed) proxies; AS backtest from 1973

data_needs: daily (for month-end) dividend-adjusted closes for SPY, EFA/IEFA, IEF, VNQ, DBC/PDBC, BIL
3-month T-bill rate/total return for cash before BIL
pre-ETF index proxies back to 1972 (10 months of history before a 1973 start)
earliest_etf_start: 2007 (BIL May-2007; risky assets all available from DBC Feb-2006)
plain_english: Split the portfolio into five equal slices: US stocks, foreign stocks, Treasuries, real estate and commodities. Each month, keep a slice in its asset only if that asset is above its 10-month average price; otherwise park that slice in T-bills.
notes: Verified against Faber 2013 update (buy rule: monthly price > 10-month SMA; sell to cash when below; signals updated only at month-end; total-return series; cash = 90-day T-bills; equal 20% weights; FAQ: rebalanced monthly). AS confirms the 20% slices, 10-month MA, cash, and monthly full rebalance (tax-efficient TAA post) and a 1973 backtest start. Faber's original (and AS's) treatment of 'price' is the total-return/adjusted series. Equality case (close == SMA) unspecified; treat as not above. Faber also tested alternatives (10y bonds as cash, leverage) not used by AS.

name: Global Tactical Asset Allocation 13 (GTAA 13 / GTAA Moderate)
author: Mebane Faber

source.title: A Quantitative Approach to Tactical Asset Allocation, February 2013 update (Extension 1: More Asset Classes; 'GTAA Moderate')

rebalance: monthly; signal at the close of the last trading day of the month, traded at that close; all slices reset to target weights monthly
signal: TREND_i = 1 if P_i,t > SMA10_i,t (10 most recent month-end dividend-adjusted closes incl. current), else 0.
rules: Fixed target weights (Faber 2013): US large-cap value IWD 5%, US large-cap momentum MTUM 5%, US small-cap value IWN 5%, US small-cap momentum 5% (AS proxy: IWM per its Agg post; see notes), intl developed EFA 10%, emerging EEM 10%, US 10y Treasuries IEF 5%, intl 10y government bonds BWX 5%, US corporate bonds LQD 5%, US 30y Treasuries TLT 5%, commodities DBC 10%, gold GLD 10%, REITs VNQ 20%.
At each month-end close, for each asset: if close > 10-month SMA, hold its full target weight; otherwise move that asset's slice to cash (BIL).
No cross-sectional ranking; slices are independent and never redistributed to other assets.
Hold until the next month-end; rebalance every slice to its target weight monthly.
Apply AS 2025 ETF changes if replicating current AS: IWD->VTV, IWN->VBR, EFA->IEFA, EEM->IEMG; DBC->PDBC (stitched ~Dec 2022).

parameters.small_cap_momentum_mapping: IWM (uncertain; AS's 2019 matrix shows no IWM for GTAA 13)

pre_etf_proxies.IWD/MTUM/IWN/small-cap mom: Fama-French portfolios in Faber's paper (AS says it uses more accurate, undisclosed proxies instead)
pre_etf_proxies.IEF/BWX/LQD/TLT: Global Financial Data series (US 10y, foreign 10y, US corporate, US 30y)

data_needs: month-end dividend-adjusted closes for the 13 ETFs (+ BIL)

pre-ETF proxies: factor-style US equity series (value, momentum, small value, small momentum), MSCI EAFE/EM, 10y/30y Treasury, intl govt bond, US corporate bond, GSCI, gold, NAREIT total-return series
plain_english: A 13-slice global portfolio (stocks by style and region, several kinds of bonds, commodities, gold and real estate), each slice with a fixed weight. Every month a slice stays invested only if its asset is above its 10-month average; otherwise that slice sits in T-bills.
notes: Weights and asset list verified from the 2013 SSRN update (table on p.43/49: 5,5,5,5,10,10,5,5,5,5,10,10,20). AS has no public rules post for GTAA 13, but its Agg 3/6 post describes the same 13-asset universe and says the original GTAA 13 controlled how much each asset category could take (consistent with fixed weights). AS's 2019 public matrix shows GTAA 13 holding BWX, DBC, EEM, EFA, GLD, IEF, IWD, IWN, LQD, MTUM, TLT, VNQ + Cash (12 ETFs, no IWM), whereas Agg 3/6 includes IWM as the stand-in for US small-cap momentum. So the mapping of the 5% small-cap-momentum slice in AS's GTAA 13 is unverified (IWM, or folded into another ETF such as MTUM/IWN) (uncertain). The 10-month SMA is assumed to apply per asset as in GTAA 5 (paper describes the extension as the same timing model on more assets). Handling of assets before data exists (AS excludes EEM pre-1989 and BWX pre-mid-2002 in Agg) is not documented for GTAA 13 (uncertain: slice to cash vs redistributed).

name: Global Tactical Asset Allocation – Aggressive 3 (GTAA Agg 3)
author: Mebane Faber

source.title: A Quantitative Approach to Tactical Asset Allocation, February 2013 update (Extension 3: GTAA Aggressive); ranking method from 'Relative Strength Strategies for Investing' (2010)

rebalance: monthly; signals at the close of the last trading day of the month, traded at that close; full rebalance monthly even without position changes
signal: MOM_i = (r1 + r3 + r6 + r12)/4 with r_k = P_t/P_{t-k months} - 1 on month-end dividend-adjusted closes (P_t = current month-end close, so r1 includes the latest month). TREND_i = 1 if P_t > SMA10 (10 month-end adjusted closes incl. current).
rules: At the close on the last trading day of the month compute MOM_i (simple average of 1, 3, 6 and 12-month total returns) for each of the 13 assets.
Rank assets by MOM_i descending and select the top 3 (relative momentum). Tie-break not specified (use deterministic order, e.g. higher r12).
Each selected asset gets a fixed 1/3 slice. If a selected asset's close is below its 10-month SMA, its 1/3 slice goes to cash (BIL) instead; the slice is NOT passed to the 4th-ranked asset.
Hold until the last trading day of the next month; rebalance the whole portfolio monthly.
Assets lacking history are excluded from ranking (AS: EEM excluded before 1989, BWX before mid-2002).
AS 2025 ETF changes: IWD->VTV, IWN->VBR, EFA->IEFA, EEM->IEMG; DBC->PDBC (~Dec 2022).

parameters.momentum_weighting: equal average of the four total returns
parameters.weighting: equal 1/3 per selected asset; failing trend filter -> that slice to cash
parameters.small_cap_momentum_proxy: IWM (AS: no qualifying US small-cap momentum ETF)

pre_etf_proxies.note: Faber used Fama-French data for equity sleeves; AS uses its own more conservative (undisclosed) proxies; AS backtest from 1981

data_needs: month-end dividend-adjusted closes for the 13 ETFs and BIL (13 months of history needed for r12, 10 for SMA)
pre-ETF proxies for each asset class back to ~1980
plain_english: Each month, rank 13 global asset classes by their average return over the last 1, 3, 6 and 12 months and put a third of the portfolio in each of the top three. Any of those three that has fallen below its 10-month average is replaced by T-bills for that third.
notes: Rules taken from the AS post and verified against Faber 2013 (top 6 or top 3 of 13 ranked on average of 1/3/6/12-month total returns; only held if above long-term MA, else that portion to cash). AS notes the absolute-momentum filter binds only ~5% of months for Agg 3. AS results are well below the paper's, which AS attributes mainly to Fama-French proxies in the original. Faber's 2010 RS paper used a 1/3/6/9/12 combination for its own tests, but the 2013 paper (and AS) use 1/3/6/12. Tie-breaking unspecified. AS live-trading nuance: signals use the closing auction print; a tiny price difference vs last real-time price once flipped an Agg 6 slice (AS 'when the close is not really the close' post).

name: Global Tactical Asset Allocation – Aggressive 6 (GTAA Agg 6)
author: Mebane Faber

source.title: A Quantitative Approach to Tactical Asset Allocation, February 2013 update (Extension 3: GTAA Aggressive)

rebalance: monthly; signals at the close of the last trading day of the month, traded at that close; full rebalance monthly
signal: MOM_i = (r1 + r3 + r6 + r12)/4, r_k = P_t/P_{t-k} - 1 on month-end dividend-adjusted closes (current month-end included). TREND_i = 1 if P_t > SMA10 of month-end adjusted closes (incl. current).
rules: At the month-end close compute MOM_i for the 13 assets.
Select the 6 assets with the highest MOM_i (tie-break unspecified).
Each selected asset gets a fixed 1/6 slice; if it closes below its 10-month SMA its 1/6 goes to cash (BIL), not to the 7th-ranked asset.
Hold until next month-end; rebalance the full portfolio monthly.
Exclude assets without history (AS: EEM before 1989, BWX before mid-2002); same 2025 ETF substitutions as Agg 3.

parameters.weighting: equal 1/6 per selected asset; failing trend filter -> cash

pre-ETF index proxies back to ~1980
plain_english: Same as the Agg 3 version, but it holds the six strongest of the 13 asset classes, one sixth each. Any of the six that is below its 10-month average is swapped for T-bills.
notes: Identical to Agg 3 except top_n = 6 and 1/6 slices (AS post). Faber's 2013 paper presents top-6 as the main Aggressive model and top-3 as a variant. AS: trend filter changes allocations in ~20% of months for Agg 6. AS documented a real-time vs official-close discrepancy on 11/30/2021 that moved ~17% from cash to TLT in Agg 6.

name: The Trinity Portfolio (Lite)
author: Mebane Faber (Cambria Investment Management)

source.title: The Trinity Portfolio (Cambria white paper; AS links Trinity_WP_122816_A.pdf, dated Dec 2016)

rebalance: monthly; signals at the close of the last trading day of the month, traded at that close; whole portfolio (static + dynamic halves) rebalanced monthly
signal: For each of 10 entities (US equity = MTUM+IWD composite, EFV, EEM, LQD, TLT, BWX, TIP, DBC, GLD, VNQ): MOM = (r1+r3+r6+r12)/4 on month-end dividend-adjusted closes (current month-end included); TREND = 1 if month-end close > SMA of last 10 month-end adjusted closes.
rules: Static half (50% of portfolio, % of TOTAL portfolio): MTUM 4.50, IWD 4.50, EFV 6.75, EEM 2.25, LQD 9.90, TLT 6.75, BWX 7.20, TIP 0.90, DBC 2.50, GLD 2.50, VNQ 2.25 (sums to 50%).

Dynamic half (50%): at the month-end close score each of 10 entities by the average of 1, 3, 6 and 12-month total return; MTUM and IWD are treated as ONE US-equity entity (always selected/filtered together).

Select the top 5 entities (top half). Each gets a fixed 10% slice (one fifth of the dynamic half) if its close is above its 10-month SMA; otherwise that 10% goes to cash (BIL). A US-equity selection is split between MTUM and IWD (presumably 5%/5%) (uncertain).
AS 2% minimum-position rule: when TIP is not selected by the dynamic half, its 0.9% static allocation is moved to TLT (so TLT static becomes 7.65%).
Final weight per ETF = static weight + any dynamic slice; hold until the next month-end; rebalance monthly.
Current AS tickers: EEM->IEMG and IWD->VTV after 2025 changes; DBC->PDBC (~Dec 2022).

parameters.us_equity_composite: MTUM+IWD treated as one entity; composite return construction not disclosed by AS (50/50 assumed) (uncertain)
parameters.min_position_rule: positions < 2% not allowed; TIP 0.9% -> TLT when TIP not selected

pre_etf_proxies.note: AS backtest from 1976; proxies not disclosed

author_original_tickers.intl equity: individual stocks with value tilt (AS: EFV)
author_original_tickers.intl treasuries: selected sovereign bond markets via Faber's sovereign-bond methodology (AS: BWX)

pre-ETF proxies back to 1975 (US momentum and value factor series, intl value, EM, corp bonds, long Treasuries, intl govt bonds, TIPS proxy, commodities, gold, REITs)
plain_english: Half the money sits permanently in a global market-style mix of stocks, bonds, commodities, gold and real estate (with value and momentum tilts). The other half is invested each month in the five strongest of those assets by recent momentum, 10% each, but only if each is above its 10-month average; otherwise that 10% sits in T-bills.

AS calls it 'Lite' because it replaces the white paper's individual-stock factor exposures (US momentum/value, intl value) with MTUM/IWD/EFV and Faber's sovereign-bond selection with BWX, and expands 10 asset classes to 11 ETFs. Original Cambria white paper could not be retrieved (links 404) so the paper's own weights/versions (e.g., different static/dynamic splits) are unverified. Ambiguities: how the MTUM+IWD composite momentum/SMA is computed (AS offers the math on request only); whether TIP's 0.9% also moves to TLT when TIP is selected but fails its SMA (likely, since the rule is about sub-2% positions) (uncertain); tie-breaks unspecified.

name: 12-Month High Switch [Dynamic Bond]
author: Mebane Faber

source.title: 12-Month High Switch Model (Meb Faber; AS does not cite the specific publication)

rebalance: monthly; signal at the close of the last trading day of the month, traded at that close; rebalance monthly even with no change
signal: H12_i,t = max of month-end dividend-adjusted closes over months t-11..t (current estimated close + preceding 11 month-ends). NEAR_HIGH_i = 1 if P_i,t >= 0.95 * H12_i,t (i.e. within 5% of the 12-month high).
rules: At the close on the last trading day of the month compute H12 for SPY, EFA (IEFA from 2025), VNQ, GLD and commodities (DBC, PDBC from ~Dec 2022).
Allocate a fixed 20% to each of these five assets whose month-end close is within 5% of its 12-month high.

Pool the unallocated 20% slices into the defensive sleeve. AS-tracked Dynamic Bond version: put the pool in IEF only if IEF is itself within 5% of its own 12-month high; otherwise put the pool in cash (BIL).
Original (non-tracked) version: unallocated slices always go to IEF.
Hold until the next month-end; rebalance monthly.
Before an asset has sufficient history, split the portfolio evenly among the remaining assets (AS calc note; commodities data from 12/1969, VNQ proxy from 12/1971).

parameters.dynamic_bond: IEF subject to same within-5%-of-12-month-high test, else cash
parameters.weighting: fixed 20% per qualifying risk asset; remainder to IEF/cash

pre_etf_proxies.note: AS backtest from 1970 using undisclosed index proxies; PDBC data history extended back to 12/1969, VNQ to 12/1971

author_original_tickers.note: same five asset classes Faber uses in GTAA (US stocks, foreign stocks, REITs, commodities) except gold replaces bonds as a risk asset; bonds are the switch asset

data_needs: month-end dividend-adjusted closes for SPY, EFA/IEFA, VNQ, GLD, DBC/PDBC, IEF, BIL
pre-ETF proxies back to ~1969 (S&P 500 TR, EAFE TR, REIT TR, gold, commodity index TR, 10y Treasury TR, T-bills)
plain_english: Five assets (US stocks, foreign stocks, real estate, gold, commodities) each get 20% only when they are trading within 5% of their highest month-end price of the past year. Money not used goes to intermediate Treasuries, but only if Treasuries are also near their 12-month high; otherwise it waits in T-bills.
notes: AS tracks ONLY the Dynamic Bond variant on its platform (stated in AS post). Original Faber publication not identified/verified (AS links mebfaber.com, SSRN 962461 and cambriafunds.com/insights generically). 'Within 5%' interpreted as P >= 0.95*H12; equality and whether the high uses closes only (yes, month-end closes per AS) are as stated by AS. AS lists commodities as PDBC in this 2024 post (DBC stitched to PDBC).

name: Sector Relative Strength
author: Mebane Faber

source.title: Relative Strength Strategies for Investing (Cambria working paper, April 2010)

signal: MOM_i = average of 1, 3, 6, 9 and 12-month total returns on month-end dividend-adjusted closes (Faber 2010 'combination' ranking) (uncertain whether AS uses 1/3/6/9/12 or 1/3/6/12). HEDGE = 1 if S&P 500 (SPY) month-end close < its 10-month SMA (uncertain).
rules: At the month-end close rank the US sector ETFs by MOM_i (trailing total-return momentum).
Select the top 3 sectors and weight them equally (1/3 each) (uncertain: paper reports Top 1, Top 2 and Top 3 variants; AS's choice not public).

Dynamic hedge (paper's version): if the S&P 500 closes below its 10-month SMA, move the entire portfolio to cash (T-bills/BIL) (uncertain whether AS uses this market-level filter or a per-sector 10-month SMA filter; the paper says both give similar results).
A sector that drops out of the top N is sold at the monthly rebalance and replaced by the new top-N member.
Hold until the next month-end; rebalance monthly.

plain_english: Each month, buy the US stock-market sectors that have risen the most over the past year (blending several look-back periods) and hold them equally. When the overall market is in a downtrend (below its 10-month average) the strategy steps aside into T-bills.
notes: LOW CONFIDENCE ON AS SPECIFICS. AS has no public rules post for this strategy (the AS 'Sector Rotation with Fama-French Alphas' post is an unrelated, rejected strategy). AS's 2019 matrix confirms only that it trades 'US Sectors (Multiple)' plus Cash. Rules above follow Faber's 2010 paper (verified): rank 10 sectors on trailing total returns over 1-12 months or the average of 1/3/6/9/12; hold top 1/2/3 equally; optional dynamic hedge to 100% T-bills when S&P 500 < 10-month SMA (or per sector). AS's exact sector list, lookback combination, number held and filter design are NOT verified. Faber also suggests a sell filter (buy top 3, sell when out of top 5) to cut turnover; not known to be used by AS.

name: Tactical Yield
author: Mebane Faber

source.title: T-Bills and Chill...Most of the Time (Cambria Investments white paper, Feb 2025)

rebalance: monthly; signals at the close of the last trading day of the month, traded at that close; rebalanced monthly even with no change
signal: TERM_t = Y10_t - Y3M_t; CREDIT_t = YIG_t - Y3M_t (month-end yields). TERM_ON = 1 if TERM_t is in the top half of all observations of TERM up to and including t (expanding window, i.e. TERM_t > expanding median); CREDIT_ON likewise for CREDIT_t.
rules: At the close on the last trading day of the month compute the term premium (10-year Treasury yield minus 3-month T-bill yield) and the credit premium (investment-grade corporate bond yield minus 3-month T-bill yield).
Compare each premium with its own full history up to that date (no look-ahead).
If the term premium is in the top half of its history, allocate 50% to IEF; otherwise that 50% stays in cash (BIL).
If the credit premium is in the top half of its history, allocate 50% to LQD; otherwise that 50% stays in cash.
Hold until the next month-end; rebalance monthly.

parameters.history_window: expanding, all data to date (AS: 30y/50y rolling windows gave similar results)
parameters.weighting: fixed 50% per sleeve; failing sleeve -> cash

pre_etf_proxies.LQD: US investment-grade corporate bond total return series

name: Robust Asset Allocation – Balanced (RAA Balanced)
author: Wesley Gray (Alpha Architect), with Jack Vogel and David Foulke

rebalance: monthly; signals at the close of the last trading day of the month, traded at that close; slices reset monthly
signal: For each asset i: MA_i = 1 if P_i,t > SMA12_i,t (12 month-end dividend-adjusted closes incl. current) else 0; TMOM_i = 1 if 12-month total return of i > 12-month total return of T-bills else 0. EXPOSURE_i = (MA_i + TMOM_i)/2 in {0, 0.5, 1} (uncertain details).
rules: Target weights (uncertain, not verified from source): US equity 20% split value IWD 10% / momentum MTUM 10%; international equity 20% split value EFV 10% / EFA 10% (stand-in for intl momentum); US REITs VNQ 10%; commodities DBC 10%; 7-10y Treasuries IEF 40%.
At each month-end compute the two trend rules per asset: price above its 12-month SMA, and 12-month total return above the T-bill return over the same 12 months.
Hold target_weight x 1.0 if both rules are positive, x 0.5 if exactly one is positive, x 0 if neither (uncertain); the de-risked portion goes to cash (BIL).
Trend rules assumed to apply to every sleeve including IEF (uncertain).
Hold until next month-end; rebalance all sleeves monthly.
AS 2025 ETF changes: IWD->VTV, EFA->IEFA; DBC->PDBC (~Dec 2022).

parameters.weighting: fixed strategic weights scaled by trend exposure; remainder to cash

name: Adaptive Asset Allocation
author: Adam Butler, Michael Philbrick, Rodrigo Gordillo (GestaltU / ReSolve Asset Management)

source.title: Adaptive Asset Allocation: A Primer

rebalance: monthly; signal computed and traded at the close of the last trading day of the month; whole portfolio rebalanced every month even if holdings are unchanged
signal: MOM_i = P_t / P_{t-126} - 1 on daily dividend-adjusted closes (126 trading days ~ 6 months). Weighted covariance for the selected assets: Sigma = D * C126 * D, where D = diag(sigma_i), sigma_i = std dev of the last 20 daily returns, and C126 = Pearson correlation matrix of the last 126 daily returns.
rules: At the close on the last trading day of the month compute MOM_i for all 10 assets.
Rank by MOM_i and select the top 5 (the top half of the universe). No absolute-momentum filter: the 5 are held even if their momentum is negative; there is no cash.
Before RWX data exist (AS: until mid-1999) the universe is 9 assets and the top 4 are selected (keeps the top-half rule).
Build Sigma = D*C126*D for the selected assets (20-day volatility, 126-day correlation).
Solve the long-only minimum-variance portfolio: minimise w' Sigma w subject to sum(w) = 1 and w_i >= 0.
AS practical filter: any weight below 2% of the portfolio is set to zero and its weight is redistributed proportionally to the remaining positions.

name: Tactical Permanent Portfolio
author: Adam Butler (GestaltU / ReSolve Asset Management)

source.title: Permanent Portfolio Shakedown Part II (GestaltU)

rebalance: monthly; all calculations use data as of the close one trading day BEFORE the last trading day of the month; trades executed at the close of the last trading day; whole portfolio rebalanced monthly
signal: Evaluated at T-1 (day before the month's last trading day): TREND_i = Close_{T-1} > SMA_200(daily closes ending T-1). sigma_i = std dev of the last 21 daily returns ending T-1. Portfolio vol = sqrt(252 * w' Sigma60 w), Sigma60 = sample covariance of the last 60 daily returns ending T-1 (annualisation by sqrt(252) assumed).
rules: On the trading day before the last trading day of the month (T-1), keep those of SPY, IEF and GLD whose close is above their 200-day simple moving average.
Weight the kept assets by simple inverse volatility: w_i = (1/sigma_i) / sum_j(1/sigma_j), sigma from 21-day daily returns as of T-1.
Compute the annualised volatility of this risk-parity portfolio from the 60-day covariance matrix as of T-1.
If portfolio volatility > 7%, scale all weights by 7%/vol and put the remainder in cash. If <= 7%, keep weights summing to 100% (AS uses no leverage).
If no asset is above its 200-day SMA, hold 100% cash.
Execute at the close of the last trading day of the month (T); hold until the last trading day of the next month.

name: Defensive Adaptive Asset Allocation (KDA)
author: Ilya Kipnis (QuantStrat TradeR)

source.title: Right Now It's KDA...Asset Allocation (QuantStrat TradeR blog)

signal: MOM_i = 12*(p0/p21 - 1) + 4*(p0/p63 - 1) + 2*(p0/p126 - 1) + (p0/p252 - 1), p_k = dividend-adjusted close k trading days ago (unnormalised 13612W sum). Covariance for min-var: Sigma = D*C*D with D = diag(std dev of last 21 daily returns) and C = (12*C21 + 4*C63 + 2*C126 + C252)/19, Ck = Pearson correlation of the last k daily returns.
rules: At the month-end close compute MOM for the 10 investment assets, the canaries EEM and AGG, and IEF.
Canary: if MOM_EEM > 0 and MOM_AGG > 0, risk-on share R = 100%; if exactly one is > 0, R = 50%; if neither, R = 0%.
Investment sleeve: rank the 10 investment assets by MOM, take the top 5, and discard any of them with MOM <= 0.

If 2+ assets remain, weight them by long-only, fully invested minimum variance using the weighted covariance Sigma; if exactly 1 remains it gets the whole sleeve; if none remain the sleeve goes to cash (per Kipnis' code; AS does not state this case).
Multiply sleeve weights by R.
Crash-protection share (1 - R): allocate to IEF if MOM_IEF > 0, otherwise to cash. IEF can also be held in the investment sleeve; weights add.
AS filter: positions below 2% of the portfolio are dropped and reallocated proportionally to the other positions.
Trade at the close; hold until the last trading day of the following month.

name: Minimum Correlation Portfolio
author: David Varadi (CSS Analytics), with Michael Kapler, Henry Bee, Corey Rittenhouse

source.title: The Minimum Correlation Algorithm: A Practical Diversification Tool

rebalance: monthly, last trading day close (AS default; AS reports ~96 small trades/yr = 8 assets x 12 months)
signal: Over a lookback of L daily returns (L = 60 trading days, uncertain): C = Pearson correlation matrix, sigma_i = std dev of daily returns. MinCorr: mu_rho, s_rho = mean and std dev of the N(N-1)/2 off-diagonal correlations; A_ij = 1 - NormCDF(rho_ij; mu_rho, s_rho) for i != j, A_ii = 0; a_i = mean_{j != i} A_ij; rank r_i with the highest a_i (least correlated) = rank 1 and the lowest a_i (most correlated) = rank N; q_i = r_i / sum(r); v_j = sum_i q_i * A_ij; v normalised to sum 1; final w_j = (v_j / sigma_j) / sum_k(v_k / sigma_k).
rules: At the month-end close take the last L daily dividend-adjusted returns of the 8 ETFs.
Compute the correlation matrix and each asset's volatility.
Transform correlations into the 'adjusted' matrix A_ij = 1 - NormCDF(rho_ij, mean, sd of all off-diagonal correlations).
Average each row of A (excluding the diagonal), rank the averages so that the most-correlated asset gets the largest rank, and convert ranks to rank weights q = r/sum(r).
Multiply rank weights by A (q' A), normalise to sum to 1, divide by each asset's volatility and renormalise to 100%.
Long-only, always fully invested in all 8 assets; no trend filter, no cash. (Special cases in reference code: 1 asset -> 100%; 2 assets -> inverse volatility.)
Trade at the close and hold until the next month-end.

name: Percentile Channels
author: David Varadi (CSS Analytics)

source.title: A Simple Tactical Asset Allocation Portfolio with Percentile Channels (for Dummies)

rebalance: monthly; weights computed and traded at the close of the last trading day of the month; whole portfolio rebalanced monthly
signal: For each asset i and lookback L in {60,120,180,252} trading days: UP = 75th percentile and LO = 25th percentile of the last L daily closes. State S_{i,L}: becomes +1 when Close > UP, becomes -1 when Close < LO, otherwise keeps its previous value (hysteresis, tracked daily). Score_i = (sum over the 4 lookbacks of S_{i,L}) / 4. sigma_i = std dev of the last 20 daily returns.
rules: Track the 16 asset/lookback channel states daily (entry above the 75th percentile, exit below the 25th percentile).
At the month-end close compute Score_i = average of the 4 states (values -1, -0.5, 0, 0.5, 1).
Compute C_i = Score_i / sigma_i (20-day volatility).
Compute W_i = |C_i| / sum_j |C_j|, where the denominator includes assets with negative scores.
Set W_i = 0 for assets with negative (or zero) score; the strategy is long-only.
Cash = 1 - sum(W_i).
Trade at the close; hold until the next month-end.

parameters.weighting: channel score x inverse volatility, normalised by the sum of absolute values across all 4 assets; negatives zeroed; residual to cash
parameters.percentile_method: linear interpolation (R quantile type 7 / numpy default) assumed; window includes the current close in the reference code (uncertain for AS)

name: Diversified Dual Momentum
author: Corey Hoffstein (Newfound Research)

source.title: Fragility Case Study: Dual Momentum GEM

rebalance: monthly, last trading day close (AS default, assumed); Newfound rebalanced the 7-model blend annually
signal: For each lookback L in {6,7,8,9,10,11,12} months: R_i(L) = P_t / P_{t-L months} - 1 on month-end dividend-adjusted closes (i = SPY, EFA); hurdle H(L) = T-bill total return over the same L months (BIL / 3-month T-bill).
rules: At the month-end close, for each of the 7 lookbacks L = 6..12 months run Antonacci's GEM decision:
Absolute momentum: if R_SPY(L) > H(L), hold whichever of SPY and EFA has the higher R(L) (relative momentum); otherwise hold AGG.
Each of the 7 sub-portfolios is allocated 1/7 of capital; sum the sub-portfolio holdings to get final weights (multiples of 1/7 across SPY, EFA, AGG).

signal: Data month d = previous calendar month (1-month publication lag). RRSFS_YoY = RRSFS_d / RRSFS_{d-12} - 1; INDPRO_YoY = INDPRO_d / INDPRO_{d-12} - 1. RECESSION = (RRSFS_YoY < 0) OR (INDPRO_YoY < 0). TREND_UP = SPY_close_t > SMA_10(month-end closes t-9..t), including the current month-end close.

Compute the year-over-year change of each series for month m-1 versus month m-13.
If both YoY changes are positive: no recession signal; hold 100% SPY regardless of price trend.

If either YoY change is negative: recession signal; check trend. If SPY's month-end close is above its 10-month simple moving average of month-end closes (current month included), hold 100% SPY; otherwise hold 100% cash (3-month T-bills).
Execute at the same close; hold until the last trading day of the following month.
Alternate (non-month-end) trading days in AS use data lagged one further month (m-2).

author: Paul Novell (Investing for a Living)

source.title: A Trend Following Bond Portfolio for Any Environment (GTAA Bond 3)

name: TrendYCMacro
author: Ďurian and Radovan Vojtko (Quantpedia)

source.title: Avoid Equity Bear Markets with a Market Timing Strategy

rebalance: monthly; signal and trade at the close of the last trading day of the month; hold until the next month-end
signal: Daily excess return XS_d = r_SPY,d - r_BIL,d (adjusted closes). Excess-return index I_d = prod(1+XS). TREND_SMA = I_t > mean(I over last 200 trading days incl. today). RACHEV = mean(XS_d over last 200 days with XS_d > median of those 200) / ( -1 * mean(XS_d over last 200 days with XS_d < median) ); TREND_RR = RACHEV > 1 (Rachev ratio RR(0.5,0.5)). YC = 10y UST yield > 3m UST yield at month-end. MACRO = [YoY(RRSFS) > 0] AND [YoY(INDPRO) > 0] AND [YoY(HOUST) > 0], where YoY uses the observation for the PREVIOUS month: X_{m-1}/X_{m-13} - 1 (1-month publication lag). LONG_m = (LONG_{m-1} AND MACRO_m) OR (TREND_SMA_m AND TREND_RR_m AND YC_m).
rules: At the close of the last trading day of month m, compute YoY change of RRSFS (real retail & food services sales), INDPRO (industrial production) and HOUST (housing starts) using the data point for month m-1 vs month m-13 (vintage/as-first-available data where possible).
If all three YoY changes are > 0 AND the strategy is currently long SPY, stay 100% SPY (macro strength can only maintain, never initiate, a long position).

Otherwise compute, from daily SPY returns in excess of BIL (T-bill) returns: (a) excess-return index above its 200-day simple average; (b) 200-day Rachev ratio RR(0.5,0.5) > 1; (c) 10-year Treasury yield > 3-month Treasury yield.
If (a), (b) and (c) are all true, go/stay 100% SPY at the close.
If neither the macro-persistence condition nor the full trend+yield-curve condition holds, move 100% to cash (AS: BIL-destined funds are held as cash earning 13-week T-bill return).
Hold until the close of the last trading day of the following month.

name: Pragmatic Asset Allocation
author: Radovan Vojtko and Javorská (Quantpedia)

source.title: Pragmatic Asset Allocation Model for Semi-Active Investors

rebalance: 4 annual tranches (25% each) traded at the close of the last trading day of Jan, Apr, Jul, Oct (one tranche per date) using signals from the prior month-end (Dec, Mar, Jun, Sep); whole portfolio rebalanced monthly to target weights
signal: At signal month-end s (month before trade): MOM12_i = P_s / P_{s-12} - 1 on dividend-adjusted month-end closes; SMA12_i = mean(P_{s-11..s}) (12 month-end closes incl. s); UP_i = P_s > SMA12_i. YC_OK = 10Y UST yield > 3M UST yield at month-end s (AS: actual month-end values).
rules: Split the portfolio into 4 independent tranches of 25%. Tranche k trades only once per year, at the close of the last trading day of its month (1, 4, 7 or 10), using data as of the end of the previous month (12, 3, 6 or 9).
For the trading tranche: if the yield curve is inverted (10Y <= 3M at the signal date), send the whole 25% tranche to the defensive step.

Otherwise rank ACWI, QQQ, EEM by MOM12 descending. For each of the top two only: if UP_i, allocate 12.5% of the total portfolio to it; if not, that 12.5% goes to the defensive step (the 3rd-ranked asset never substitutes).

Defensive step for the amount D sent to defense: rank IEF, GLD, BIL by MOM12 descending; each of the top two receives D/2 if UP_i, otherwise its D/2 goes to cash. BIL allocations are held as cash (AS convention). A tranche can therefore hold up to 3 assets (1 risky + 2 defensive).

Stop-loss on the other three (non-trading) tranches at each tranche date (months 1,4,7,10): for every asset they hold, if the asset's prior month-end close < its SMA12 (as of prior month-end) AND it has been held more than 12 months, sell that slice to cash and keep it in cash until that tranche's next scheduled trade.
Every month-end, rebalance all holdings back to their target fraction of the whole portfolio (simplifying assumption of the authors, matched by AS).
All trades at the close of the last trading day of the month.

parameters.yield_curve: AS: month-end 10Y vs 3M; authors: FRED GS10 vs TB3MS (monthly averages)
parameters.weighting: fixed fractions (12.5% per risky slot; defensive split in halves)

Positions are designed to be held at least a year for tax efficiency, with a quarterly trend check as a safety valve.

name: Optimal Trend Following
author: Valeriy Zakamulin and Javier Giner

source.title: Optimal Trend Following Rules in Two-State Regime-Switching Models

rebalance: monthly; signal and trade at the close of the last trading day of the month
signal: IND_t = sum_{k=1..30} w_k * r_{t-k+1}, where r_t is the S&P 500 monthly total return (dividend-adjusted month-end closes) for the month ending at t (k=1 = most recent month). LONG if IND_t > 0. Approximate weights w_k digitized from the authors' chart (label 'NB(4) weights', scale irrelevant): k1 0.0925, k2 0.0739, k3 0.0582, k4 0.0443, k5 0.0325, k6 0.0221, k7 0.0136, k8 0.0061, k9 0.0000, k10 -0.0046, k11 -0.0082, k12 -0.0107, k13 -0.0125, k14 -0.0136, k15 -0.0139, k16 -0.0143, k17 -0.0139, k18 -0.0132, k19 -0.0125, k20 -0.0118, k21 -0.0107, k22 -0.0096, k23 -0.0089, k24 -0.0079, k25 -0.0068, k26 -0.0057, k27 -0.0050, k28 -0.0043, k29 -0.0032, k30 -0.0025.
rules: At the close of the last trading day of each month, compute the weighted sum of the last 30 monthly total returns of the S&P 500 using the optimal weights (positive for lags 1-8, ~0 at lag 9, negative for lags 10-30).
If the indicator is positive, hold 100% SPY; otherwise hold 100% cash (13-week T-bill return).
Hold until the close of the following month.

name: US Cross-Asset Momentum
author: Aleksi Pitkäjärvi, Matti Suominen, Lauri Vaittinen

source.title: Cross-asset signals and time series momentum (Journal of Financial Economics)

rebalance: monthly; signal near and trade at the close of the last trading day of the month
signal: XS_SPY = R12(SPY) - R12(BIL); XS_IEF = R12(IEF) - R12(BIL), where R12 = P_t/P_{t-12} - 1 on dividend-adjusted month-end closes (BIL = 3-month T-bill).
rules: At month-end compute 12-month excess returns of SPY and IEF over T-bills.
If XS_SPY > 0 and XS_IEF > 0: hold 100% SPY.
Else if XS_SPY < 0 and XS_IEF > 0: hold 100% IEF.
Otherwise (IEF excess return <= 0): hold 100% cash.
Hold until the close of the following month.

parameters.weighting: 100% in a single asset or cash

pre_etf_proxies.BIL: 3-month T-bill (AS backtest from 1954; specific proxy series not stated)

3-month T-bill total return series

plain_english: Holds US stocks when both stocks and Treasuries have beaten cash over the past year, holds Treasuries when bonds are up but stocks are down, and otherwise sits in cash. It uses the finding that rising bond prices are good news for stocks while strong stocks are bad news for bonds.
notes: AS tests a simplified long-only, unlevered, US-only version; the paper trades long/short across many international markets, combining own-asset TSMOM with cross-asset signals (bond past returns positive predictor for equities; equity past returns negative predictor for bonds). name: US Risk Parity Trend-Following
author: Andrew Clare, James Seaton, Peter N. Smith, Stephen Thomas

source.title: The Trend is Our Friend: Risk Parity, Momentum and Trend Following in Global Asset Allocation

rebalance: monthly; signal and trade at the close of the last trading day of the month; full rebalance every month
signal: Simple risk parity (Asness, Frazzini & Pedersen): RPW_i = (1/sigma_i) / sum_j(1/sigma_j), sigma_i = volatility of asset i's returns over the trailing 12 months, computed over all 5 assets regardless of trend. TREND_i = P_i,t > SMA10_i, SMA10 = mean of the last 10 month-end closes including the current one; P is the cash (non-dividend-adjusted) price for SPY, IWM, VNQ.
rules: At the close of the last trading day of each month, compute 12-month volatility for SPY, IWM, IEF, DBC, VNQ and set inverse-volatility weights summing to 100%.
For each asset: if its close is above its 10-month SMA, hold its risk-parity weight; otherwise hold that weight in cash (13-week T-bill).
Hold until the last trading day of the following month; rebalance the whole portfolio monthly even if signals are unchanged.

parameters.vol_return_frequency: not stated (daily or monthly returns; uncertain)
parameters.weighting: inverse volatility (no correlations), fixed slot per asset; failing trend -> slot to cash

For each slice holding its risk asset: if the risk asset's close is below its lower channel, switch the slice to its defensive asset at that close.

source.title: J.P. Morgan Efficiente Index methodology (index brochure/rulebook linked by AS; link now returns 404)

rebalance: monthly; optimise at the close of the last trading day of the month, trade at that close; full rebalance monthly regardless of changes
signal: Using the trailing 126 trading days (6 months) of daily total returns: mu_i = expected return estimate from that window (e.g. mean daily return annualised; AS does not state the exact estimator), Sigma = sample covariance of daily returns (annualised). Solve max_w w'mu subject to sqrt(w'Sigma w) <= 10% annualised, w_i >= 0, sum(w) = 1 (cash included as an asset), asset caps and group caps.
rules: At each month-end close collect 126 trading days of daily total returns for the 12 ETFs plus cash (T-bill).
Solve the long-only, unlevered mean-variance problem: maximise expected return subject to annualised realised portfolio volatility <= 10% and the caps below.

Asset caps: SPY 20%, IWM 10%, EFA 20% (group US/developed equities <= 50%); TLT 20%, LQD 20%, HYG 20% (group US bonds <= 50%); EEM 20%, EMB 20% (group emerging markets <= 25%); VNQ 20%, DBC 10%, GLD 10% (group real assets <= 25%); TIP 50%, cash 50% (group TIPS + cash <= 50%).
AS deviation: drop any weight below 2% and redistribute it proportionally across the remaining holdings (AS ignores the original rule that weights are integer multiples of 5%).
Trade at the same close and hold until the next month-end.

parameters.pre_etf_proxies: not stated by AS (backtest from 1989; EMB/HYG/DBC/GLD/TIP need index or simulated histories)
parameters.as_ticker_changes: DBC stitched to PDBC (~end 2022); EFA->IEFA and EEM->IEMG in early 2025 (AS site-wide)

data_needs: daily dividend-adjusted closes for SPY, IWM, EFA, EEM, VNQ, DBC, GLD, TLT, LQD, HYG, EMB, TIP
daily 3-month T-bill rate for the cash asset
a constrained quadratic/convex optimiser
plain_english: Every month, a portfolio optimiser picks the mix of 12 asset-class ETFs and cash that would have earned the most over the last six months while keeping volatility under 10%, subject to caps on each asset and each asset group. Because it uses such a short window, it behaves like a momentum strategy that also rewards low volatility and low correlation.
notes: Constraint table transcribed from the AS post image (20180130.04.png). AS says published versions of the index differ slightly and the description is light on detail; AS 'captured the best mix'. Not specified by AS: the exact expected-return estimator, the covariance estimator, and what happens if no portfolio meets the 10% volatility cap (possible because cash is capped at 50%); JPM index documents reportedly handle infeasibility by raising the vol target stepwise - unverified here. The JPM PDF linked by AS now returns 404; the rulebook could not be retrieved. JPM's own ETF-based versions (e.g. the one behind ETF EFFE) may use different ETFs and a different vol target (unverified). Goldman Sachs' Momentum Builder Multi-Asset index is described by AS as nearly identical.

name: Defense First
author: Thomas Carlson

source.title: Defense First: A Multi-Asset Tactical Model for Adaptive Downside Protection

rebalance: monthly; signals at the close of the last trading day of the month, traded at that close; full rebalance monthly
signal: MOM_i = (R1+R3+R6+R12)/4 with Rn = P_t/P_{t-n months} - 1 on month-end dividend-adjusted closes, for i in {TLT, GLD, PDBC, UUP, BIL}. BIL momentum is the hurdle only.
rules: At the month-end close compute MOM for TLT, GLD, PDBC, UUP and BIL.
Rank the four defensive assets by MOM from highest to lowest and assign slot weights 40%, 30%, 20%, 10% by rank.
For each slot: if the asset's MOM < MOM_BIL, give that slot's weight to SPY instead; otherwise hold the asset at the slot weight.
SPY weight = sum of all redirected slots (0%-100%); SPY's own momentum is not checked.
Trade at the same close; hold until the next month-end; rebalance monthly even if unchanged.

parameters.hurdle: BIL (13-week T-bill) momentum, strict less-than sends slot to SPY
parameters.pre_etf_proxies: not stated by AS (backtest from 1971; requires gold, commodity index, US dollar index and T-bill histories)
parameters.as_ticker_notes: AS represents commodities with DBC stitched to PDBC (~end 2022)

data_needs: month-end dividend-adjusted closes for TLT, GLD, PDBC/DBC, UUP, BIL, SPY
pre-ETF: long Treasury TR, gold spot, commodity index TR, US Dollar Index (plus collateral yield for UUP-like returns), T-bill TR
plain_english: The strategy ranks four defensive assets (long Treasuries, gold, commodities, US dollar) by recent momentum and gives them 40/30/20/10% of the portfolio. Any defensive asset that is doing worse than T-bills hands its share to US stocks, so stocks are owned mainly when defensive assets are weak.
notes: Rules from AS; the SSRN paper returned HTTP 403 and could not be checked directly. Ties in ranking and the case MOM == MOM_BIL are not addressed (AS wording 'less than' implies equality keeps the defensive asset). AS suggests (but did not implement) holding cash instead of UUP because UUP contributed almost nothing after costs, and considering a cap on stock exposure when stock momentum is negative; neither is part of the tracked rules. AS reports that results were benchmark-like after ~1980 with lower drawdowns and low correlation to other TAA strategies.

name: Hybrid Asset Allocation 60/40
author: NLX Finance (variant of Keller & Keuning's HAA-Simple)

source.title: NLX Finance HAA 60/40 variant (original publication not located); base strategy: Keller & Keuning, 'Dual and Canary Momentum with Rising Yields/Inflation: Hybrid Asset Allocation (HAA)'

rebalance: monthly; signals and trades at the close of the last trading day of the month; rebalanced monthly even without a signal change
signal: MOM_i = (R1+R3+R6+R12)/4 (unweighted), Rn = P_t/P_{t-n months} - 1 on month-end dividend-adjusted closes, for TIP, SPY, IEF and BIL (BIL = cash-momentum proxy).
rules: At the month-end close compute MOM for TIP and SPY.
If MOM_TIP > 0 and MOM_SPY > 0 (risk on): hold 60% SPY + 40% IEF.
Otherwise (either is negative): if MOM_IEF > MOM_BIL hold 100% IEF, else 100% cash.
Trade at the same close; hold to next month-end; rebalance to target weights monthly.

parameters.risk_off: IEF if MOM_IEF > MOM_BIL else cash
parameters.cash: AS replaces BIL holdings with cash (3-month T-bill return)

pre_etf_proxies.TIP: IEF used in place of TIPS before end-1973 (as in the HAA paper); simulated TIPS 1974-2003 (AS caveat on data quality)

data_needs: month-end dividend-adjusted closes for SPY, TIP, IEF
T-bill total return (BIL or 3-month T-bill) for the cash hurdle and cash return
earliest_etf_start: 2003-12 (TIP; BIL Jun 2007 only if the ETF is used for the hurdle)
plain_english: When both TIPS and US stocks have positive average momentum, hold a 60/40 mix of stocks and intermediate Treasuries; otherwise hold intermediate Treasuries if they beat T-bills, or cash if not. It is a calmer version of Keller's HAA-Simple, which holds 100% stocks when risk is on.
notes: AS gives no rules beyond 'identical to HAA-Simple except 60% SPY / 40% IEF when risk on'; the full rule set above is taken from AS's HAA-Simple post. NLX Finance's own publication could not be located (no link in the AS post; nlxfinance.com does not resolve; web search unavailable). The treatment of exactly-zero momentum is unspecified. AS ran an adversarial test replacing TIPS with IEF before the TIP ETF; results were in line with the original test.

name: Dividend & Growth Allocation (DGA)
author: Paul Choi

source.title: Balance Between Growth and Dividend: Dividend & Growth Allocation

rebalance: monthly; signals and trades at the close of the last trading day of the month; hold to next month-end
signal: Risk-on requires all three: (C1) TIP_t > SMA12(TIP month-end closes); (C2) DY_t = D12_{m-1} / SPX_t >= 1.6%, where D12 = trailing-12-month S&P 500 dividends per share as of the previous month (1-month lag) and SPX_t = current S&P 500 price index; (C3) for none of the monthly observations 7 through 15 months before t is the curve inverted, inverted meaning (10y UST yield - 3m UST yield) < -0.50 pp. Risk-on momentum: MOM_i = (R1+R3+R6+R9+R12)/5 on month-end closes. Risk-off momentum: MOM_i = P_t / SMA6(month-end closes) - 1.
rules: At the month-end close evaluate C1, C2 and C3; risk on only if all three pass.
Risk on: compute MOM (average of 1, 3, 6, 9, 12-month % returns) for QQQ and SCHD; hold 100% of the higher one.
Risk off: compute MOM = close / 6-month SMA of month-end closes - 1 for BIL, TLT and PDBC; if the highest MOM is positive hold 100% of that asset, otherwise hold cash.
Any allocation to BIL is held as cash (AS convention).
Trade at the same close; hold until the last trading day of the next month.

parameters.pre_etf_proxies: not stated by AS (backtest from 1974; SCHD launched 2011, QQQ 1999, TIP 2003, PDBC 2014/DBC 2006 - AS uses simulated/index histories)
parameters.author_original_tickers: QQQ, SCHD, TIP, BIL, TLT, PDBC as used by AS (author's exact tickers not re-verified)

data_needs: month-end dividend-adjusted closes for QQQ, SCHD, TIP, TLT, PDBC/DBC, BIL
S&P 500 price index and trailing-12-month dividends per share (quarterly S&P data or Shiller dataset), dividend lagged 1 month
FRED T10Y3MM from June 2019 onward; before June 2019 AS computes the 10y-3m spread from underlying yield series (exact series not stated, e.g. GS10/TB3MS)
plain_english: The strategy is fully invested in either Nasdaq-100 or high-dividend US stocks, whichever has stronger momentum, but only when TIPS are in an uptrend, the S&P 500 dividend yield is at least 1.6%, and the yield curve has not been deeply inverted 7-15 months earlier. Otherwise it holds the strongest of T-bills, long Treasuries and commodities, or cash if none is trending up.
notes: AS revised its post on 01/10/24 after the author revised the paper on SSRN (01/03/24) to define inversion as the 10y yield at least 0.5% below the 3m yield. AS found the yield-curve rule fragile: FRED's T10Y3MM methodology changed in June 2019, so AS self-computes the spread before that date and uses T10Y3MM afterwards. AS's monthly TIP SMA presumably uses month-end closes (price vs adjusted not stated). AS criticises the fixed 1.6% dividend-yield threshold as fit to post-1990s history and shows an adversarial version (IEF instead of simulated TIPS pre-ETF, no dividend-yield check, from 1970). Tie handling unspecified. SSRN page returned 403, so the paper was not checked directly.

name: Paired Switching Strategy
author: Lewis Glenn (per AllocateSmartly); the paired-switching concept was published by A. Maewal & J. R. Bock (2011) - relationship unverified

source.title: Paired-Switching for Tactical Portfolio Allocation (Maewal & Bock, SSRN working paper) - attribution of AS's 'Glenn' version unverified

rebalance: quarterly at the last trading day of each calendar quarter (uncertain - see notes; AS may evaluate monthly)
signal: R_i = P_t / P_{t-3 months} - 1 on dividend-adjusted closes for i in {SPY, TLT} (lookback uncertain); hold argmax R_i. Relative momentum only - no absolute filter.
rules: At each rebalance date compute the trailing (3-month, uncertain) total return of SPY and TLT.
Hold 100% of whichever has the higher return (ties unspecified); never cash.
Hold until the next rebalance date.

parameters.pre_etf_proxies: not stated (S&P 500 TR and long-term Treasury TR expected)

data_needs: month-end dividend-adjusted closes for SPY and TLT (index proxies pre-2002)
plain_english: Always fully invested in either US stocks or long-term Treasuries, whichever has performed better recently. Because the two usually move in opposite directions, the switch tends to catch whichever is in favour.
notes: No dedicated public AS post. Confirmed from AS public material: the pair is SPY and TLT (AS 2019 strategy-asset matrix), the strategy uses only relative momentum with no absolute filter (AS 'Dynamic Bond' post, 11/2023), and its trading-cost drag was 0.65%/yr (2019). The lookback (3 months / prior quarter) and quarterly switching come from recollection of the Maewal & Bock paper and could not be verified (SSRN returned 403; web search quota exhausted). Inference: 0.65%/yr at 0.1% per trade implies about 3.25 full switches per year, which would require switching in ~80% of quarters under strict quarterly rebalancing; that is more consistent with a monthly check of a multi-month lookback, so AS's implementation frequency is genuinely uncertain. AS also lists Lewis Glenn as author of Quint Switching Filtered (SSRN 3129098), so 'Glenn' may be a later author of the paired-switching approach rather than the 2011 authors.

name: Quint Switching Filtered (QSF)
author: Lewis Glenn

source.title: Quint Switching Filtered (Lewis Glenn, SSRN working paper; exact title not verified)

rebalance: monthly; signals and trades at the close of the last trading day of the month
signal: R3_i = P_t / P_{t-3 months} - 1 on month-end total-return closes for i in {SPY, QQQ, EFA, EEM, TLT}.
rules: At the month-end close compute 3-month total return for SPY, QQQ, EFA, EEM and TLT.
If any of the five has R3 < 0: hold 100% IEF.
If all five have R3 > 0: hold 100% of the asset with the highest R3 (ties unspecified; exactly-zero returns unspecified).
Trade at the same close; hold until the last trading day of the next month.

parameters.filter: all five risk assets must have positive 3-month return
parameters.pre_etf_proxies: not stated by AS (AS backtest from 1970 requires Nasdaq-100 and MSCI EM proxies/simulations before their index inception)

data_needs: month-end dividend-adjusted closes for SPY, QQQ, EFA, EEM, TLT, IEF (daily if modelling alternate trading days)
plain_english: Look at five markets (US large caps, Nasdaq-100, developed international, emerging markets and long Treasuries). Only if all five have risen over the past three months, buy the strongest one; otherwise sit entirely in intermediate Treasuries, which happens about three months out of four.
notes: Rules from AS; the SSRN paper (abstract 3129098) returned 403 and was not checked directly. 'Filtered' refers to the all-positive requirement; an unfiltered 'Quint Switching' presumably holds the top 3-month performer of the five unconditionally (inferred from the name, unverified). The requested link to Scott's Investments' 'Quint Switching' could not be checked (scottsinvestments.com is now a parked domain; web search unavailable). AS notes TLT acts mainly as a spoiler (held ~2.4% of months), very high exposure to rising rates and extreme timing luck (alternate trading days CAGR 8.5%-14.8%). AS also tracks a '[Dynamic Bond]' variant (from 11/2023) that applies the momentum rule to IEF and goes to cash if it fails (presumably IEF R3 > 0 - exact form not published).

name: Global Growth Cycle (GGC)
author: Grzegorz Link

source.title: Global Growth Cycle (grzegorz.link)

rebalance: monthly on the 15th calendar day (or the next trading day) at the close; hold until the next 15th
signal: DI = (number of countries whose CLI rose month-over-month) / (number of countries with data), using each country's OECD Composite Leading Indicator for the most recent month available (the month ending before the trade month, i.e. CLI_{m-1} vs CLI_{m-2} when trading in month m). Individual countries only; regional aggregates (EA19, G-7, OECD, OECDE, etc.) excluded. Earliest-vintage CLI values. Risk on if DI >= 0.5.
rules: On the 15th calendar day of each month (or the first trading day after), compute DI from the previous month's CLI data for all individual countries available at that time.
If DI >= 0.50, hold 100% SPY at the close; otherwise hold 100% cash (3-month T-bill return).
Hold until the 15th of the next month.

parameters.trade_day: 15th calendar day or next trading day
parameters.cli_reference_month: previous calendar month (released in the first ~2 weeks of the trade month)
parameters.cli_vintage: earliest available vintage per data point (AS official results)
parameters.country_set: all individual countries in the OECD CLI at the time (~43 before the 2023 OECD overhaul; 17 after)
parameters.cli_series_variant: OECD country CLI (amplitude-adjusted series assumed - not specified by AS or the author; uncertain)

pre_etf_proxies.SPY: S&P 500 total return (AS backtest from 1956 with revised data; vintage-based official results)

data_needs: OECD Composite Leading Indicator by country, monthly, with historical vintages (OECD vintages unavailable before 2001)
daily dividend-adjusted SPY closes
3-month T-bill rate for cash
plain_english: Each month, check what share of countries have a rising OECD leading economic indicator. If at least half are rising, own the S&P 500; otherwise hold cash.
notes: AS's first test (12/2021) replicated the author's revised-data backtest from 1956 (lookahead bias, since each new CLI data point revises the entire history) and then showed a vintage-based test; AS official results use the earliest vintage. Vintaging is imperfect: OECD vintages are missing before 2001 and constituent-country changes before 12/2021 cannot be vintaged (survivorship). The 2023 OECD overhaul cut the CLI to 17 countries; AS's 08/2023 re-test found similar long-run results (agreement ~83% of months). The author's page uses price-only S&P 500 with no costs, cash return or dividends, shifts each DI value 15 days, and presents an alternate version that switches to a 50-day moving-average rule when DI < 0.5 (AS did not replicate it). Exact handling of countries with missing data in a month is not specified.

name: Global Growth Cycle Enhanced (GGC Enhanced)
author: Grzegorz Link

source.title: Global Growth Cycle enhanced with momentum (grzegorz.link)

rebalance: monthly, last trading day close (AS 'Monthly' version); AS also tracks a 'Mid-Month' version that trades on the 15th calendar day
signal: DI as in GGC (share of countries whose OECD CLI rose month-over-month, using the previous month's CLI data - 1-month reporting lag - earliest vintage). Risk on if DI > 0.5 (strict). R12_i = P_t / P_{t-12 months} - 1 on month-end dividend-adjusted closes for SPY, IEFA, AGG, BIL.
rules: At the close on the last trading day of month t, take OECD CLI values for month t-1 (the most recent month, published in the first 1-2 weeks of month t) and month t-2 for every individual country (exclude regional aggregates such as EA19, G-7, OECD, OECDE).
Diffusion Index = share of those countries whose CLI rose month-over-month.
If DI > 0.5 (strictly greater) the strategy is risk on: compare 12-month returns of SPY and IEFA and put 100% in the higher one.
If DI <= 0.5 the strategy is risk off: if AGG's 12-month return exceeds BIL's, put 100% in AGG; otherwise 100% cash (BIL).
Trade at that close and hold until the last trading day of the following month.
Mid-Month variant: on the 15th calendar day (or next trading day) compute the DI from the CLI month just released (the previous month) and apply the same rules; hold until the next 15th.

parameters.cli_vintage: earliest vintage (imperfect for constituent changes before 12/2021)
parameters.pre_etf_proxies: not stated (AS monthly backtest from 1961, mid-month from 1973; IEFA presumably EFA/MSCI EAFE before 2012 - uncertain)

author_original_tickers.AGG: aggregate bonds per the author's flowchart; the author's article text also mentions IEF vs BIL in the risk-off branch (discrepancy unresolved)

parameters.country_universe: individual OECD countries only (exclude regional aggregates such as EA19, G-7, OECD); 39 countries before 2022, 17 since

data_needs: OECD CLI by country with vintages, 1-month reporting lag
month-end dividend-adjusted closes for SPY, IEFA (EFA pre-2012), AGG, BIL (or 3-month T-bill total return)
earliest_etf_start: 2003-09 (AGG; EFA 2001; IEFA itself Oct 2012; BIL 2007 only if the ETF is used for the hurdle)
plain_english: The same global leading-indicator test decides between risk on and risk off. When risk is on, it holds whichever of US or international stocks has the better 12-month return; when risk is off, it holds US aggregate bonds if they beat T-bills over 12 months, otherwise cash.
notes: Rules and author flowchart from the AS post (12/2025, flowchart image 20251128.06.png). The author's article (fetched) uses VXUS for international stocks and a 12-month lookback in backtests; its text describes the risk-off branch as IEF vs BIL while the flowchart shown by AS says 'Agg Bonds > T-Bills' - AS uses AGG. The > vs >= threshold difference was unintentional by the author; it matters only when an even number of countries can give exactly 0.5 (currently 17 countries). AS did not separately quantify the vintage-data impact for this version. | Additional detail: Author's own version: risk-on SPY vs VXUS, risk-off IEF vs BIL (author says he preferred AGG but his data source lacked it), lookback 12 months (found best by author, who flags possible overfitting); author's page does not clearly state the risk-off lookback or the exact execution day. AS uses AGG vs BIL and SPY vs IEFA. The author notes 39 countries before 2022 and 17 since (odd counts, so > vs >= currently identical). AS vintages each country's data points but cannot vintage historical changes in the country list before 12/2021, so some lookahead remains. Whether 12-month returns are dividend-adjusted is not stated (AS normally uses total return).

name: Momentum Based Balancing
author: Mark Virag

source.title: Momentum Based Balancing for the Diversified Portfolio (NAAIM Wagner Award paper)

rebalance: monthly; signal and execution at the close of the last trading day of the month; all positions reset to target weights every month
signal: R3_i = P_t / P_{t-3m} - 1 on month-end dividend-adjusted closes (AS convention) for the 9 ETFs; R3_cash = 0 by definition (cash is treated as a 10th asset with zero momentum). Baseline B = second-lowest of the 10 R3 values. Score S_i = max(R3_i - B, 0). Weight w_i = S_i / sum_j S_j.
rules: At the close on the last trading day of month t, compute the 3-month total return of SPY, IWM, XLB, EFA, EEM, VNQ, IEF, TLT, TIP; assign cash a 3-month return of exactly 0.
Sort the 10 values and take the second-lowest value as baseline B (B is usually negative).
For every asset (including cash) compute S_i = R3_i - B; any S_i below zero (i.e. the single lowest asset) is set to 0. The second-lowest asset therefore also ends with 0.
Sum all S_i; weight of each asset (including cash) = S_i / sum S.
Edge case not specified by AS: if sum S = 0 (all 10 returns identical) allocate 100% to cash (implementer choice). Ties at the bottom simply produce several zero weights.
Execute all trades at the same close; hold until the last trading day of the next month, then recompute and rebalance to new weights (full monthly rebalance even if ranks unchanged).
Cash portion earns the 3-month T-bill rate (AS 'cash' convention), even though its signal return is fixed at 0.

pre_etf_proxies.XLB: AS diversified-commodities series (DBC/PDBC proxy) before ~late 1989, because AS lacks materials-sector data earlier
pre_etf_proxies.others: AS index-based asset-class histories (not itemised in post)

parameters.author_original_tickers: not stated by AS (paper not retrieved); AS notes the author chose XLB rather than DBC because DBC lacked history when the paper was written

data_needs: month-end dividend-adjusted closes for SPY, IWM, XLB, EFA (IEFA), EEM (IEMG), VNQ, IEF, TLT, TIP
3-month T-bill rate (FRED DTB3/TB3MS) for cash return
commodity index series to proxy XLB before ~1989 if extending pre-ETF
earliest_etf_start: 2005 (VNQ launched Sep 2004; TIP Dec 2003; EEM Apr 2003)
plain_english: Each month the strategy looks at how nine stock, real-estate and bond ETFs plus cash did over the last three months. It shifts every return up so the second-worst asset sits at zero, drops the worst, and then allocates money in proportion to each asset's shifted return, so recent winners get the biggest slices.
notes: AS backtest from 1973. AS describes the paper as a 2014 NAAIM Wagner Award winner; the NAAIM award page lists different 2014 top-3 winners, so the award status could not be confirmed and the paper itself was not retrieved (rules here come from AS's post, which gives a worked numeric example that matches the formula above). Price vs total return for the 3-month return is not stated explicitly; AS generally uses dividend-adjusted data with a 2-day dividend lag. Because rank-proportional weighting concentrates in whichever group (risk-on or bonds) is leading, AS also showed an Optimum-3-style variant, but that is not the tracked version.

name: Excess Earnings Yield Dynamic - Valuation Only
author: James White and Victor Haghani (Elm Wealth)

source.title: Man Doth Not Invest by Earnings Yield Alone

rebalance: monthly; signal and execution at the close of the last trading day of the month; rebalance to target every month even if unchanged
signal: EY_t = 1 / CAPE_q where CAPE_q is Shiller's CAPE for the most recent calendar quarter-end month that is at least 3 months before t; RY_t = 10-year TIPS real yield at t (decimal); EEY_t = EY_t - RY_t; w_SPY = clip(EEY_t / (gamma * sigma^2), 0, 1) with gamma = 2 and sigma = 0.18, i.e. w_SPY = clip(EEY_t / 0.0648, 0, 1); w_TIP = 1 - w_SPY.
rules: On the last trading day of month t, look up Shiller CAPE (10-year inflation-adjusted earnings) for the latest quarter-end month (Mar/Jun/Sep/Dec) that is at least 3 months earlier than t (AS's own anti-lookahead lag; e.g. at end-July use March CAPE, at end-September use June CAPE).
Earnings yield EY = 1 / CAPE.
Take the current 10-year TIPS real yield RY (month-end value; decimal).
Excess earnings yield EEY = EY - RY.
Equity weight (Merton rule) = EEY / (2 * 0.18^2); floor at 0%, cap at 100% (no shorting, no leverage).
Remainder (1 - equity weight) goes to TIP. There is no cash/T-bill option.
Execute at the close; hold to the next month-end; rebalance monthly regardless of change.

parameters.cape_lag: most recent quarter-end CAPE at least 3 months old (AS addition)

pre_etf_proxies.TIP: AS simulated TIPS returns before 1997 (method not disclosed)
pre_etf_proxies.TIPS_real_yield: AS simulated historical real yields before TIPS existed (method not disclosed)

author_original.sigma: authors' main method: dynamic vol = sqrt(0.75 * life-to-date average of rolling 10y variance + 0.25 * recent 2y variance) of monthly S&P 500 returns; constant 0.18 offered by authors as an optional simplification which AS uses
author_original.real_yield_history: Elm: actual US 10y TIPS 1997+, UK 10y index-linked gilts 1985-1997, nominal 10y UST minus inflation expectations minus 0.5% before 1985

data_needs: Shiller monthly CAPE (Shiller online data, ie_data.xls)
10-year TIPS real yield: FRED DFII10 (daily, from 2003); 1997-2002 needs another source (e.g. Fed H.15 historical / Gurkaynak-Sack-Wright real curve) (uncertain which AS uses); simulated pre-1997
month-end dividend-adjusted closes for SPY and TIP
pre-ETF: S&P 500 TR index and a simulated TIPS return series
plain_english: Compares the long-run real return you can expect from US stocks (1/CAPE) with the guaranteed real yield on 10-year TIPS. The bigger the stock advantage, the more goes into stocks, using a textbook formula that scales the advantage by stock risk; the rest sits in TIPS.
notes: AS text renders the denominator as '2 * 0.182'; the superscript was lost: AS footnote says 0.18 is annual stock volatility and Elm's formula is mu/(gamma*sigma^2) with gamma=2 (Elm's worked example 5%/(2*20%^2)=62.5%), so the denominator is 2*0.18^2=0.0648. AS backtest from 1973; AS simulates TIPS returns and real yields pre-1997 and warns these are educated guesses. AS states the authors helped clarify rules. Exact TIPS-yield series and whether month-end or lagged value is used are not stated by AS. Elm's paper did not state rebalance frequency for main backtests (turnover figures assume monthly).

name: Excess Earnings Yield Dynamic with Momentum
author: James White and Victor Haghani (Elm Wealth)

source.title: Man Doth Not Invest by Earnings Yield Alone

rebalance: monthly; signal and execution at the close of the last trading day of the month; rebalance to target every month even if unchanged
signal: EEY_t = 1/CAPE_q - RY_t (as in valuation-only). Momentum: for k = 0..11 take SPY dividend-adjusted month-end close P_{t-k} and form D_{t-k} = P_{t-k} / (CPI_{t-k}/CPI_ref) / 1.04^((t-k - ref)/12) (i.e. deflated by CPI and by a constant 4%/yr risk-premium growth path). MOM = +1 if D_t > mean(D_{t-11..t}) else -1. EEY*_t = EEY_t + 0.02*MOM. w_SPY = clip(EEY*_t / (2*0.18^2), 0, 1); w_TIP = 1 - w_SPY.
rules: Compute EEY exactly as in the valuation-only variant (1/CAPE from latest quarter-end CAPE at least 3 months old, minus 10-year TIPS real yield).
Take the 12 most recent month-end dividend-adjusted closes of SPY (including the current month-end).
Discount each by cumulative inflation (CPI) and by a constant 4% annual risk premium, producing a real, premium-adjusted series of 12 values.
If the latest discounted value exceeds the simple average of the 12 discounted values, add 0.02 to EEY; otherwise subtract 0.02.
Equity weight = adjusted EEY / (2 * 0.18^2), floored at 0 and capped at 1; remainder to TIP.
Execute at the close; hold until next month-end; rebalance monthly.

Else if slope < its 10-year median: regime = Inflation. Portfolio: 50% SPY, 10% IWN, 40% GLD.
Else (HY spread below median and slope above median): regime = Slowdown. Portfolio: 50% LQD, 40% IEF, 10% IWN.
Rebalance to the regime portfolio at that close; the regime holds until the next month-end close.
