rules: At the close on the last trading day of the month, check whether ACWI's month-end close is a new all-time high versus all previous month-end closes.
If yes, hold 100% ACWI from that close; otherwise hold 100% AGG.
Hold until the last trading day of the following month.

parameters.high_definition: all-time high of month-end values (price vs total-return series not specified - uncertain)

pre_etf_proxies.ACWI: GFD global stock data before 1970 (gross of foreign withholding taxes), global index data after (AS)
pre_etf_proxies.AGG: intermediate US Treasuries (IEF proxy) before 1968; US aggregate bond index after

data_needs: monthly close of ACWI or global equity index (long history from GFD/MSCI)
monthly adjusted close AGG or US aggregate bond index
plain_english: Owns global stocks only in months when they have just closed at a record high; the rest of the time it owns US bonds. It holds stocks less than 30% of the time.
notes: Faber's post describes the rule generically (stocks at all-time high -> stocks next month, else government bonds); AS chose ACWI and AGG. Whether the all-time high is measured on price or total return is not stated (AS normally uses dividend-adjusted data; uncertain). Tie (equal to prior high) treated as a high here - not specified. AS used this as an illustration that new highs are not a reason to avoid stocks; results depend heavily on bond returns.

name: Lazy Man's Momentum Strategy (country rotation)
author: Not verified (SSRN working paper 5644131)

source.title: Lazy Man's Momentum Strategy (SSRN 5644131; exact title/authors not verified)

rebalance: semi-annually, at the close of the last trading day of June and December

risky: 22 country equity indices (list per source paper; not given by AS, not verified)

signal: MOM6_i = P_i(t) / P_i(t-6m) - 1 on month-end closes (total return presumed)
rules: At the end of June and December, rank the 22 country indices by 6-month return.
Hold the 11 highest-ranked countries in equal weight (1/11 each), regardless of whether their returns are positive.
Hold for six months until the next rebalance.
Optional (AS robustness check): split into 6 tranches rebalanced semi-annually in different month pairs (Dec/Jun, Jan/Jul, ...); AS found essentially identical results.

parameters.pre_etf_proxies: MSCI country indices (AS backtest from 1971; uncertain)

data_needs: monthly total-return series for the 22 country indices (MSCI) or iShares country ETFs
ACWI for benchmark
earliest_etf_start: 1996 (most iShares MSCI country ETFs launched 03/1996) - depends on the unverified country list
plain_english: Twice a year it buys the half of 22 national stock markets that rose the most over the previous six months, in equal amounts. AS found the momentum selection has added nothing versus picking the losers since about 2000; most of the long-run edge came from equal weighting.
notes: Source paper not retrievable (SSRN 403) - authors, country list and return convention unverified. AS will not add it: relative performance vs the inverse (bottom-11) strategy has been flat since mid-2000. AS floated, but did not test, an absolute-momentum variant (send negative-momentum slots to cash).

name: Front-Running Commodity Seasonality (with correlation filter)
author: Cyril Dujava (Quantpedia)

source.title: Trader's Guide to Front-Running Commodity Seasonality

rebalance: monthly, last trading day close
signal: For month t (positioning for t+1): s = t-10 (the same calendar month as t+1, one year earlier; author's 'X-11'). PCT_i = percentile rank of r_i(s) within ETF i's own monthly returns from s through t (AS: 'all months since'; Quantpedia: the last 12 monthly returns). SIDE_i = +1 if PCT_i >= 50th percentile else -1. Correlation filter: C_S = average pairwise correlation of daily returns of the 4 ETFs over the last 20 trading days, C_L = same over the last 250 trading days; RISK_OFF = C_S > C_L.
rules: At each month-end, for each ETF take its return in the month 11 months before the month being positioned for (e.g. at end-December use the previous February).
Rank that return against the ETF's own monthly returns since then; at or above the median -> long, below -> short.
Base version: +/-25% of capital in each ETF (net exposure between -100% and +100%).
Risk-parity variant: size each position inversely to its trailing 36-month volatility (scaling to 100% gross assumed - uncertain).
Correlation-filter variant: if the 20-day average pairwise correlation exceeds the 250-day average, hold 100% cash for the month.
Long-only variant (AS Test #3, includes the correlation filter): short signals become cash (each ETF slot 25%).
Hold all positions until the next month-end.

pre_etf_proxies.DBA,DBB,DBE,DBP: Deutsche Bank (DBIQ) commodity sector indices when available, otherwise similar Bloomberg and S&P GSCI sub-indices (AS backtest from 1990)

data_needs: daily adjusted close DBA, DBB, DBE, DBP (or DB/Bloomberg/GSCI sector index proxies)
monthly returns from the same
earliest_etf_start: 2007 (all four Invesco DB sector ETFs launched 01/2007)
plain_english: Bets that commodity seasonal patterns get traded a month early: each month it goes long or short four commodity sector funds depending on whether their return in the corresponding month a year earlier was strong or weak. A filter moves to cash when the four commodities start moving too much in lockstep.
notes: AS post lists 'DBC: Energy' - a typo for DBE (later text says DBE). Proof of concept: AS ignored transaction and shorting costs. AS found results concentrated in 2000-2010 and flat otherwise; the correlation filter improved Sharpe. Quantpedia's article gives the 20/250-day windows only in its companion momentum article; exact averaging formula (pairwise mean) not stated - uncertain. Risk-parity sizing formula not stated by AS. Long-short base is the author's design; the long-only variant is AS's.

name: Commodity Momentum/Reversal with Intra-Market Correlation
author: Margareta Pauchlyova (Quantpedia)

source.title: How to Improve Commodity Momentum Using Intra-Market Correlation

rebalance: monthly, last trading day close
signal: MOM12_i = P_i(t) / P_i(t-12m) - 1 (adjusted closes); C_S = average pairwise correlation of daily returns over the last 20 trading days; C_L = same over the last 250 trading days.
rules: At each month-end compute the 12-month return of each of the four ETFs and the short- and long-window average correlations.
If C_S > C_L (momentum regime): long the 2 ETFs with the highest 12-month return and short the 2 with the lowest.
If C_S < C_L (reversal regime, per Quantpedia): long the 2 ETFs with the lowest 12-month return and short the 2 with the highest.
Equal weights (assume +/-25% each, 100% gross - uncertain); hold for one month.
data_needs: daily adjusted close DBA, DBB, DBE, DBP (or index proxies)
plain_english: A long/short commodity sector strategy that follows momentum when the four sectors are moving together more than usual and bets on reversal when they are moving apart.
notes: AS's wording of the reversal branch appears garbled (it repeats the momentum positions); Quantpedia's article states the reversal regime goes long the 2 worst and short the 2 best, which is used here. Tie (C_S = C_L) unspecified. AS found it worked only over the author's original sample and failed in earlier years; no costs included. Long/short only.

name: Front-Running Seasonality in Country ETFs
author: Sona Beluska (Quantpedia)

source.title: Front Running in Country ETFs, or How to Spot and Leverage Seasonality

rebalance: monthly, last trading day close
signal: SCORE_i = r_i(t-10): the ETF's return in the calendar month that is 11 months before the month being positioned for (at end of March, use May of the previous year); rank cross-sectionally, descending.
rules: At the close on the last trading day of month t, rank all available country ETFs by their return in month t-10.
Select the top 8 and weight them: ranks 1-3 18.18% each, rank 4 15.15%, rank 5 12.12%, rank 6 9.09%, rank 7 6.06%, rank 8 3.03% (i.e. 6,6,6,5,4,3,2,1 /33).
Hold until the last trading day of the following month and repeat.
ETFs enter the universe only once data exist (Quantpedia added EZA, FXI, INDY after their launches).

pre_etf_proxies.all: MSCI country index data (AS backtest from 1971; country availability varies)

data_needs: monthly total-return series for the 23 ETFs or their MSCI country index proxies
plain_english: Assumes investors anticipate each country's seasonal pattern a month early. Each month it buys the 8 country funds that did best, a year ago, in the month that is now one month ahead, with larger weights for the top ranks.
notes: Quantpedia's final portfolio averages six sub-portfolios (top 3, 4, ..., 8); AS translated this into the rank weights above (AS assumption, matched their overlap closely). If each sub-portfolio were equal-weighted internally, weights would be the 'alt' set (our computation). AS results exclude transaction costs and AS declined to track (not consistently effective since 1971, esp. late 1990s). Without the front-running month (same month last year) results were worse.

name: 12-Month Momentum with Distance-to-1-Year-High Filter
author: Allocate Smartly

source.title: A Key New Momentum Measure to Consider: Distance from 1-Year High

rebalance: monthly, last trading day close
signal: MOM12 = P_t / P_{t-12m} - 1 (dividend-adjusted month-end closes); D = (P_t - min(P_{t-12..t})) / (max(P_{t-12..t}) - min(P_{t-12..t})) over 13 month-end closes including the current one; LONG = MOM12 > 0 AND D >= 0.75
rules: At the close on the last trading day of the month compute the S&P 500's 12-month dividend-adjusted price change.
Compute D, the position of the current close within the range of the last 13 month-end closes (0 = 1-year low, 1 = 1-year high).
If the 12-month change is positive and D >= 0.75, hold 100% SPY; otherwise hold T-bills.
Hold until the next month-end.

parameters.baseline_variant: drop the D filter (plain 12-month absolute momentum)

data_needs: monthly dividend-adjusted S&P 500 / SPY closes
13-week T-bill rate
plain_english: A classic rule that owns stocks when they are up over the past year, with an extra check: the market must also be in the top quarter of its 1-year price range. If it has risen over the year but fallen well off its high, it waits in cash.
notes: AS's own proof of concept (no transaction costs), inspired by Alpha Architect's coverage of an SSRN paper (abstract 2900073, title not verified) on distance from the 52-week high and momentum crashes; AS changed it to a long-only, monthly, no-skip-month index strategy. Boundary (>= vs > 0.75) not stated; AS's bucket table groups 75% with the stronger bucket. Whether D uses the same dividend-adjusted series is not stated (presumed). Revised strategy reduced drawdowns but underperformed the baseline for ~20 years from the early 1990s.

name: Aggregate Investor Allocation to Equities (AIAE) Timing
author: Philosophical Economics (Jesse Livermore, pseudonym) - indicator; Allocate Smartly - trading rule

source.title: The Single Greatest Predictor of Future Stock Market Returns

rebalance: monthly, last trading day close
signal: AIAE = E / (E + D), E = market value of corporate equities (FRED NCBEILQ027S + FBCELLQ027S), D = liabilities of real-economy borrowers (FGSDODNS + CMDEBT + BCNSDODNS + DODFFSWCMI + SLGSDODNS), all in the same units. FORECAST_t = a_t + b_t * AIAE_latest from an expanding-window OLS of subsequent 10-year annualized S&P 500 total return on AIAE, using only observations whose 10-year outcome is known at t; LONG = adjusted FORECAST_t > current T-bill yield.
rules: At the close on the last trading day of each month, take the latest published AIAE value (quarterly Federal Reserve Z.1 data; first-release vintage; may be up to ~5 months old).

Fit an OLS regression of subsequent 10-year annualized S&P 500 (dividend-adjusted) return on AIAE using all observations from inception (12/1951) whose 10-year forward return is complete by today (walk-forward, no lookahead).
Forecast the next-10-year annualized return from the latest AIAE.
Adjust the forecast for the S&P 500's move since the AIAE observation date (AS follows Micaletti; exact adjustment formula not given).
If the adjusted forecast exceeds the T-bill yield, hold 100% SPY; otherwise hold T-bills. Hold until next month-end.

parameters.regression: OLS, expanding window, y = 10-year forward annualized S&P 500 TR, x = AIAE
parameters.data_lag: up to 5 months (Z.1 quarterly release ~10 weeks after quarter end)

data_needs: FRED/ALFRED quarterly Z.1 series: NCBEILQ027S, FBCELLQ027S, FGSDODNS, CMDEBT, BCNSDODNS, DODFFSWCMI, SLGSDODNS (first-release vintages; check unit differences - millions vs billions)
Z.1 release dates
monthly S&P 500 TR / SPY
3-month T-bill yield (FRED TB3MS/DTB3)
plain_english: Measures what share of investors' total holdings is in stocks; when that share is high, future 10-year returns have tended to be low. The rule owns stocks when the indicator's forecast return beats T-bills and holds T-bills otherwise.
notes: Trading rule is AS's own simple illustration (long ~87% of the time); AS says it barely improved risk-adjusted returns and failed to avoid 2008. FRED series codes come from Portfolio Optimizer's 2023 replication (the original 2013 post defines the ratio conceptually: stocks / (stocks + liabilities of households, nonfinancial corporates, state/local and federal government, rest of world)). AS says it used monthly data in the regression though Z.1 is quarterly - how monthly AIAE values were formed (forward-fill or market-adjusted) is not stated (uncertain). The market-move adjustment method is not specified. AS also mentions but did not publish versions based on Micaletti ('Towards a Better Fed Model') and Asness et al. ('Market Timing: Sin a Little').

name: End-of-Month / Second-Half-of-Month Treasury ETF Seasonality
author: Jonathan Hartley and Krista Schwarz (paper); ETF application by Allocate Smartly

source.title: Predictable End-of-Month Treasury Returns

rebalance: calendar-based daily timing, close-to-close
signal: Variant A (EOM3): in TLT for the returns of the last 3 trading days of each month. Variant B (second half): normalize each month to 21 trading days (day 1 = first, day 21 = last); in TLT for the returns of normalized days 11-21, out on days 1-10.
rules: Variant A: buy TLT at the close of the 4th-to-last trading day of the month; sell at the close of the last trading day; otherwise out of the market.
Variant B: buy TLT at the close of normalized trading day 10; sell at the close of the last trading day (day 21); otherwise out of the market.
The same rules can be applied to IEF or SHY (effect shrinks with duration).

parameters.off_period_holding: not specified by AS (cash assumed - uncertain)

pre_etf_proxies.TLT: index DBUS20VL before mid-2002 (as named by AS)
pre_etf_proxies.IEF: Bloomberg US Treasury 7-10y TR (LT09TRUU) before mid-2002

parameters.author_original_tickers: coupon Treasury securities (excess returns over the last few days of month)

data_needs: daily adjusted close TLT (and IEF/SHY optional) or index proxies
trading calendar to identify last trading days / normalized days
plain_english: Long-term Treasury funds have tended to rise in the final days, and more broadly the second half, of each month. This calendar rule holds TLT only during those windows.
notes: AS analysis is an observation, not a recommended standalone strategy; no transaction costs. Since ~2014 the positive bias shifted from day EOM-1 to EOM-2. AS's day-normalization method (mapping months to 21 days) is described only by reference to its FAQ - reproduce approximately (uncertain). Paper abstract (Sharpe ~1 for last-few-days long) verified via Capital Spectator summary; SSRN page itself blocked.

name: Sector Rotation with Fama-French Alphas
author: Undisclosed (AS withheld the paper; rules are AS's modified version)

source.title: Undisclosed paper (title withheld by AS)

rebalance: monthly, last trading day close
signal: For each sector i: OLS over 36 month-end observations ending at month t-2 of (R_i - RF) = alpha_i + b1(Mkt-RF) + b2 SMB + b3 HML + b4 RMW + b5 CMA + e, using Fama-French 5-factor monthly data; SELECT if alpha_i > 0.
rules: At the close on the last trading day of the month, for each sector ETF regress its monthly excess returns on the five Fama-French factors over the 36 months ending two months ago (skip the two most recent months for data-release delay).
Select all sectors with a positive intercept (alpha).
Equal-weight the selected sectors; hold until the next month-end.
If no sector has positive alpha: not specified (cash assumed - uncertain).

pre_etf_proxies.sectors: S&P 500 sector indices before SPDR launch 12/1998 (AS backtest from 1993; proxy not stated)

data_needs: monthly adjusted closes of the sector SPDRs (or S&P 500 sector TR indices)
Ken French data library: Fama/French 5 Factors (2x3), monthly, incl. RF
plain_english: Each month it estimates how much of each sector's recent 3-year performance cannot be explained by standard market factors, and holds equal amounts of every sector with a positive unexplained return.
notes: AS withheld the source paper and tested 'similar in spirit' rules; the 2-month skip is AS's change for real-world data delays. The exact 10 sectors are not listed: '10 S&P Sector SPDR ETFs' in 11/2017 likely means the nine originals plus XLRE (XLC launched 2018) - uncertain. AS concluded factor alphas have little predictive power for sectors and did not track it.

name: Utilities Beta Rotation (utilities vs market relative strength)
author: Charles Bilello and Michael Gayed (identification ours; AS withheld the paper title)

source.title: An Intermarket Approach to Beta Rotation: The Strategy, Signal and Power of Utilities (2014 Charles H. Dow Award; identification not confirmed by AS)

signal: R4_X = P_X(t) / P_X(t - 4 weeks) - 1 on weekly closes; HOLD XLU if R4_XLU > R4_VTI else VTI
rules: At the close of each week compute the 4-week return of utilities (XLU) and of the total market (VTI).
If utilities' 4-week return is greater, hold 100% XLU for the next week; otherwise hold 100% VTI.
Repeat weekly.

pre_etf_proxies.VTI: CRSP US Total Market (CRSPTMT) extended with Russell 3000 TR (RU30INTR)

optional: Ken French industry and market returns for the original long test

plain_english: Each week it owns utility stocks if they have outperformed the overall market over the past four weeks (a sign of defensive positioning), otherwise it owns the whole market.
notes: AS used this as a cautionary example: strong on Ken French data from 1926 but roughly market-like on tradeable index/ETF data since 1989, and would underperform after costs. AS test excluded transaction costs. Paper identity inferred from AS's description (Dow Award winner, 4-week utilities vs market) - not confirmed; source URL not retrieved.

name: Aggregate TAA Allocation as a Trading Signal
author: Allocate Smartly

source.title: The Wisdom of 100 Strategies: Using Aggregate TAA Allocation as a Trading Signal

rebalance: monthly at month-end close (best after costs); AS also tested semi-monthly (normalized days 10 and 21), weekly (days 5/10/15/21) and daily, each with same-day or next-day (1-day lag) execution
signal: AGG_a(t) = average across all strategies tracked by AS of each strategy's current weight in asset a (AS 'Aggregate Allocation Report'; strategy weighting presumably equal - uncertain).
rules: On each rebalance date, compute the aggregate allocation across all tracked TAA strategies (by individual ticker).

Granularity options: (a) hold the aggregate weights by ticker; (b) roll up positions < 2% into generic asset classes; (c) map to categories: US equities SPY, US real estate VNQ, US gov bonds IEF, US non-gov bonds LQD, intl equities IEFA, intl real estate VNQI, intl bonds BWX, precious metals GLD, commodities PDBC, cash; currency/market-neutral categories held as cash; (d) risk on/off: equities + real estate + high-yield bonds -> SPY, everything else -> IEF (cash separate).
Trade the resulting weights at the close (same day) or at the next day's close (realistic, since the report is generated overnight).
Hold until the next rebalance date.
data_needs: daily allocations of every AS-tracked strategy (members-only on AS); can be approximated by running all tracked strategies in this catalog and averaging
daily adjusted closes for all category proxies
plain_english: Averages what all the tactical strategies AllocateSmartly follows are currently holding and simply copies that average portfolio. It acts like one very diversified tactical portfolio.
notes: NOT directly replicable: requires AS members-only aggregate data. Approximation requires implementing the full set of AS tracked strategies (which changed over time: 50+ in 2020, 100+ in 2026) and averaging; AS's averaging method (equal weight per strategy, handling of alternate trading days) is not stated. Earlier 2020 post (https://allocatesmartly.com/using-aggregate-taa-allocation-as-a-tool-for-timing-the-market/) tested the same idea with EFA/RWX/DBC proxies, without costs.
